   594	    {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) (a u : Fin L → F.K) :
   595	    binTrace F.K (dotProduct a u) =
   596	      binTrace (ZMod 2)
   597	        (dotProduct (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a) (kappaVec F u)) := by
   598	  simp only [dotProduct, map_sum, binTrace_mul_eq_dotProduct F,
   599	    Algebra.trace_self_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type, quditQubitLabelEquiv,
   600	    Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.curry_symm_apply, kappaVec, basisCoordVec]
   601	  rfl
   602	
   603	/-- The coordinate label equivalence preserves addition. -/
   604	private theorem quditQubitLabelEquiv_add {q : ℕ}
   605	    (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) (a b : Fin L → F.K) :
   606	    quditQubitLabelEquiv F L (a + b) =
   607	      quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a + quditQubitLabelEquiv F L b := by
   608	  ext p
   609	  rcases p with ⟨i, j⟩
   610	  change F.binaryCoordinates (a i + b i) j =
   611	    F.binaryCoordinates (a i) j + F.binaryCoordinates (b i) j
   612	  simp
   613	
   614	/-- A shift observable is the permutation matrix for addition by its label. -/
   615	private theorem tauObservable_X_apply
   616	    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
   617	    [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   618	    (a x y : ι → K) :
   619	    tauObservable .X a x y = if x = y + a then 1 else 0 := by
   620	  change (∏ i : ι, if x i = y i + a i then 1 else 0) = _
   621	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
   622	  have hsupport : (∀ i, x i = y i + a i) ↔ x = y + a := by
   623	    simpa only [Pi.add_apply] using
   624	      (funext_iff (f := x) (g := y + a)).symm
   625	  simp only [hsupport]
   626	
   627	/-- A phase observable is diagonal, with its phase given by the trace pairing. -/
   628	private theorem tauObservable_Z_apply
   629	    {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K]
   630	    [Algebra (ZMod 2) K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   631	    (a x y : ι → K) :
   632	    tauObservable .Z a x y =
   633	      if x = y then phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a y)) else 0 := by
   634	  change
   635	    (∏ i : ι,
   636	      if x i = y i then phaseSign (binTrace K (a i * y i)) else 0) = _
   637	  rw [Fintype.prod_ite_zero, prod_phaseSign_binTrace_dotProduct]
   638	  have hsupport : (∀ i, x i = y i) ↔ x = y :=
   639	    (funext_iff (f := x) (g := y)).symm
   640	  simp only [hsupport]
   641	
   642	/-- Binary-coordinate relabeling transports both generalized Pauli observables. -/
   643	private theorem tauObservable_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
   644	    {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ)
   645	    (W : PauliKind) (a : Fin L → F.K) :
   646	    tauObservable W a =
   647	      Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   648	        (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   649	        (tauObservable W (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a)) := by
   650	  classical
   651	  ext x y
   652	  simp only [Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm]
   653	  cases W with
   654	  | X =>
   655	      rw [tauObservable_X_apply, tauObservable_X_apply]
   656	      have hadd := quditQubitLabelEquiv_add F L y a
   657	      rw [← hadd]
   658	      by_cases hshift : x = y + a
   659	      · rw [if_pos hshift, if_pos]
   660	        exact congrArg (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L) hshift
   661	      · rw [if_neg hshift, if_neg]
   662	        exact fun h => hshift ((quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).injective h)
   663	  | Z =>
   664	      rw [tauObservable_Z_apply, tauObservable_Z_apply]
   665	      by_cases hxy : x = y
   666	      · subst y
   667	        rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl,
   668	          binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv,
   669	          quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec F L a,
   670	          quditQubitLabelEquiv_eq_kappaVec F L x]
   671	      · have hlabels : quditQubitLabelEquiv F L x ≠
   672	            quditQubitLabelEquiv F L y := fun h =>
   673	          hxy ((quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).injective h)
   674	        rw [if_neg hxy, if_neg hlabels]
   675	
   676	/-- Fourier inversion transports the Pauli projectors along the binary label
   677	equivalence. -/
   678	private theorem pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv
   679	    {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ)
   680	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin L → F.K) :
   681	    pauliProj W u =
   682	      Matrix.reindex (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   683	        (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L).symm
   684	        (pauliProj W (kappaVec F u)) := by
   685	  classical
   686	  rw [pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable, pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable]
   687	  ext x y
   688	  simp only [Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.sum_apply, smul_eq_mul,
   689	    Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm]
   690	  rw [Fintype.card_congr (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L)]
   691	  congr 1
   692	  apply Fintype.sum_equiv (quditQubitLabelEquiv F L)
   693	  intro a
   694	  have hphase := congrArg phaseSign
   695	    (binTrace_dotProduct_eq_quditQubitLabelEquiv F L a u)
   696	  have hentry := congrFun
   697	    (congrFun (tauObservable_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv F L W a) x) y
   698	  simp only [Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Equiv.symm_symm] at hentry
   699	  rw [hphase, hentry]
   700	
   701	/-- The tensor product of binary Pauli projectors, obtained by specializing
   702	`pauliProj` to `ZMod 2`. This is the binary target in `lem:pauli-binary`,
   703	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
   704	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
   705	noncomputable abbrev qubitPauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   706	    (W : PauliKind) (b : ι → ZMod 2) : Op (ι → ZMod 2) :=
   707	  pauliProj W b
   708	
   709	/-- `lem:pauli-binary`: the fixed binary coordinates induce an isometry that
   710	maps EPR states and generalized Pauli projectors to their qubit forms.
   711	Blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
   712	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`.
   713	
   714	**Local fix:** The source's final factor index is printed as
   715	`j ∈ {1, ..., q}`; the basis expansion at paper lines 1191--1194 shows that
   716	the intended range has `basisDim = log₂ q` entries. This correction is
   717	documented in `rem:pauli-binary-source` and issue #16. -/
   718	theorem exists_qubitIsometry (q : ℕ) (F : FixedFieldModel q) (L : ℕ) :
   719	    ∃ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin L → F.K) ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   720	        EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2),
   721	      isometryTensor φ.toLinearIsometry φ.toLinearIsometry
   722	          (eprState (Fin L → F.K)) =
   723	          eprState (Fin L × Fin F.basisDim → ZMod 2) ∧
   724	        ∀ (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin L → F.K),
   725	          pauliProj W u =
   726	            conjIsometry φ.symm.toLinearIsometry
   727	              (qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec F u)) := by
   728	  let e := quditQubitLabelEquiv F L
   729	  let φ := LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℂ ℂ e
   730	  refine ⟨φ, isometryTensor_piLpCongrLeft_epr e, ?_⟩
   731	  intro W u
   732	  rw [conjIsometry_piLpCongrLeft_symm]
   733	  exact pauliProj_reindex_quditQubitLabelEquiv F L W u
   734	
   735	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    17	\title{Attainment in the Symmetrization Lemma}
    18	\author{}
    19	\date{2026-08-30}
    20	
    21	\begin{document}
    22	\maketitle
    23	
    24	\section{At a glance}
    25	
    26	\begin{itemize}
    27	  \item \textbf{Difficulty: easy.}  The issue is a quantifier exchange between
    28	  a supremum and an attained maximum in a preliminary lemma on nonlocal games.
    29	  No analytic estimate is missing; the substance is deciding which statement
    30	  the symmetrization proof supports and which statement the later arguments
    31	  consume.
    32	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight:} about \textbf{1--2 lemma interfaces} and on
    33	  the order of \textbf{100--300 lines} of formal proof for the value-preserving
    34	  symmetrization construction.  The attainment step itself should not be
    35	  formalized as printed (see the Conclusion).
    36	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split:} approximately \textbf{20\% Mathlib}
    37	  (finite-dimensional inner product spaces, tensor products, block
    38	  decompositions of $\C^2 \ot \C^d$) and \textbf{80\% project-local} (games,
    39	  strategies, values, and the Naimark input).
    40	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs:} the completed projective form of
    41	  Naimark dilation, \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}, and the
    42	  definitions of symmetric games and tensor product values in the source
    43	  \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  The note is audited against the
    44	  proof-gap protocol in \ghissue{173}.
    45	\end{itemize}
    46	
    47	\section{Key theorem forms}
    48	
    49	Three statements must be kept apart.  Throughout, $\game$ denotes a symmetric
    50	two-player one-round game and $\eps \ge 0$ a real parameter; the notation is
    51	introduced in the next section.
    52	
    53	\begin{enumerate}
    54	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    55	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    56	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    57	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    58	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    59	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    60	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    61	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    62	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    63	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    64	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    65	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.
    66	\end{enumerate}
    67	
    68	The source proof consists exactly of a proof of the third form, applied to a
    69	strategy supplied by the definition of the supremum; this yields the second
    70	form.  The first form asserts strictly more than the second, and the passage
    71	from the second to the first is the gap discussed in this note.  Every use of
    72	the lemma, in the source and in this project, consumes only the second or the
    73	third form.
    74	
    75	\section{The source assertion}
    76	
    77	A two-player one-round game
    78	$\game = (\mathcal X, \mathcal A, \mu, D)$ in compact symmetric notation
    79	consists of a finite question alphabet $\mathcal X$, a finite answer alphabet
    80	$\mathcal A$, a symmetric question distribution $\mu$ on
    81	$\mathcal X \times \mathcal X$, and a decision predicate $D$ treating the two
    82	players symmetrically.  A tensor product strategy
    83	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    84	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    85	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    86	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    87	and the value of the game is the supremum
    88	\begin{equation*}
    89	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    90	\end{equation*}
    91	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
    92	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
    93	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
    94	same measurements.
    95	
    96	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    97	\footnote{The statement is at
    98	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    99	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement kept in this form
   100	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
   101	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
   102	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   103	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   104	\begin{equation*}
   105	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   106	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   107	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   108	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   109	\end{equation*}
   110	
   111	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   112	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   113	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   114	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   115	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   116	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   117	\begin{equation*}
   118	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   119	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   120	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   121	\end{equation*}
   122	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   123	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   124	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   125	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   126	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   127	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   128	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   129	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   130	
   131	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   132	
   133	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   134	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   135	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   136	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   137	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   138	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   139	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   140	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   141	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   142	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   143	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   144	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   145	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   146	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   147	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   148	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   149	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   150	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   151	form.
   152	
   153	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   154	
   155	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   156	
   157	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   158	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   159	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   160	generality that it is projective.%
   161	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   162	lines~317--321.}
   163	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   164	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   165	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   166	
   167	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   168	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   169	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   170	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   171	lines~2322--2332.}
   172	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   173	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   174	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   175	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   176	not used.
   177	
   178	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   179	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   180	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   181	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint records both forms as part of the
   182	games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on either; the two source
   183	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   184	development.
   185	Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here --- requires
   186	the attainment form.
   187	
   188	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   189	
   190	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape,
   191	as the proof-gap protocol requires when the printed statement is not known to
   192	be false and only its proof is blocked.  Its proof records the
   193	value-preserving construction and the approximate form that the construction
   194	yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment step as unproved, citing
   195	this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the obstruction.  The
   196	value-preserving given-strategy form is stated beside it as a separate
   197	formalization-support node, \path{lem:symmetric-strat-given-strategy}, which
   198	is not advertised as the source lemma.
   199	
   200	The two Lean declarations follow the same separation.  The source-shaped
   201	\leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is linked to
   202	\path{lem:symmetric-strat}; its proof is the tracked attainment obligation and
   203	remains open.  The given-strategy
   204	\leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy\_of\_strategy}, linked to the
   205	support node, has the same hypothesis, exact value equality, and projective
   206	symmetric conclusion as that node, and its proof is complete.
   207	
   208	\section{Conclusion}
   209	
   210	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   211	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   212	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   213	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built
   214	on the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   215	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   216	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   217	suffices.  Stage~4 has carried out the recommendation of this note: the
   218	given-strategy symmetrization lemma is formalized and proved as the workhorse
   219	statement, while the source-labelled lemma keeps its source shape with the
   220	attainment step an explicit, tracked proof obligation.  If a later
   221	investigation settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the
   222	statement should then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented
   223	statement correction.

    21	\section{At a glance}
    22	
    23	\begin{itemize}
    24	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low to medium.  The subtest implications are
    25	  direct after conditioning, but the printed proof uses an invalid parameter
    26	  reduction and two displayed formulas contain wrong indices.

    33	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Constant lower bounds for the
    34	  commuting and anticommuting events, data processing, and the one-way Magic

    38	
    39	\section{Key theorem forms}
    40	
    41	For an admissible tuple $(q,m,d)$ and a strategy that wins the Pauli basis test
    42	with probability at least $1-\eps$, each subtest has conditional failure
    43	$O(\eps)$.  In particular, the Magic Square average is conditioned on
    44	\[
    45	  \gamma(\omega)
    46	  =\tr\big((r_X\ind_m(u_X))\cdot(r_Z\ind_m(u_Z))\big)\ne0,
    47	\]
    48	and the low-degree line-evaluation family is completed on zero-direction lines
    49	by an additional outcome.  The observable consequence is
    50	\[
    51	  X^{r_X}(u_X)Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)
    52	  \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
    53	  (-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)X^{r_X}(u_X)
    54	\]
    55	on average over all tuples.  These statements hold for every admissible
    56	parameter tuple; no assumption $6md\leq q$ is needed.
    57	
    58	\section{The source assertions and discrepancies}
    59	
    60	The source states the measurement implications at lines~197--265 and the
    61	observable implications at lines~267--362 of the Pauli analysis
    62	\cite[lines~197--362]{Ji2020MIPStar}.%
    63	\footnote{See
    64	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.}
    65	Four corrections are required.
    66	
    67	First, the displayed conditioning event for the Magic Square average omits
    68	$\ind_m$ and writes the scalar expression
    69	$\tr((r_Xu_X)\cdot(r_Zu_Z))$, even though $u_X,u_Z\in\F_q^m$ and the phase
    70	used by the game is defined through vectors in $\F_q^{2^m}$.
    71	
    72	Second, the proof assumes $6md\leq q$ and disposes of the complementary range
    73	by appealing to the final Pauli soundness theorem, whose proof uses the lemma
    74	under discussion.  That appeal cannot prove the lemma as an unrestricted
    75	standalone result.  The corrected exact probability calculation gives
    76	universal lower bounds for both conditioning events whenever the parameters
    77	are admissible, and removes this circular reduction.%
    78	\footnote{The probability correction is documented separately in
    79	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_anticommuting-probability.tex}.}
    80	
    81	Third, the source treats evaluation classes of a line measurement as a POVM
    82	indexed by $\F_q$.  A zero-direction line admits nonconstant polynomial
    83	representatives with no well-defined value on its singleton image, so these
    84	classes form only a sub-measurement.  Adding an outcome $\bot$ for the missing
    85	mass makes the consistency relation well typed; the point family is completed
    86	by a zero effect at the same outcome.
    87	
    88	Finally, the observable proof writes
    89	$Z^{r_X}(u_X)X^{r_Z}(u_Z)$ where the intended reversed product is
    90	$Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)X^{r_X}(u_X)$.  The source label prefix
    91	\path{len:qld-win-implications-obs} is likewise a typographical error for
    92	\path{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}.
    93	
    94	\section{The corrected argument}
    95	
    96	Every question type and every relevant subtest has a universal positive
    97	sampling weight.  For admissible parameters, $1\leq m\leq q$, and the exact
    98	calculation of the anticommuting probability gives probability at least
    99	$2^{-4}$ for the anticommuting event and at least $1/2$ for its complement.
   100	Conditioning therefore enlarges rejection probabilities only by a universal
   101	factor.  The measurement implications follow directly from their rejection
   102	events, including the completed zero-direction outcome.  Data processing and
   103	the agreement identities yield the observable relations; the corrected Magic
   104	Square phase and reversed product then give the displayed signed commutation
   105	law.
   106	
   107	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   108	
   109	The blueprint uses the full phase $\gamma$, completes the line-evaluation
   110	families, proves the conditioning step with the universal probability bounds,
   111	and corrects the reversed product and label.  Its proof and correction remark
